svg.title: Company isolation: enforced in the app, and again in the database
svg.desc: Application layer: the company comes only from the X-Company-Id header; tenantMiddleware checks it with SELECT 1 FROM companies WHERE id = $1 (401 if unknown) and stores it in res.locals.ctx.companyId; the service passes it to all 10 repository functions, each of which filters or inserts by company_id. Another company’s employee returns 0 rows, so the API answers 404 EMPLOYEE_NOT_FOUND, the same as a missing id. Database layer: companies has many employees; employees exposes UNIQUE (company_id, id); probation_extensions and audit_events reference employees through the composite foreign key (company_id, employee_id), so a row pointing at another company’s employee is rejected with a foreign key violation.
svg.text: Company isolation: enforced in the app, and again in the database
Another company’s employee behaves exactly like one that does not exist. Proven by test/integration/isolation.test.ts.
The only source of the company: never the URL, never the body (bodies are strict).
service.ts passes ctx.companyId to every repository call.
all 10 functions scope their parameterised SQL
→ NotFoundError → 404 EMPLOYEE_NOT_FOUND, identical to a missing id
Backstop: a cross-company child row cannot exist
INSERT with company B's company_id and company A's employee_id
→ 23503 foreign key violation, even if the application code were wrong
